# Voiceover script (read aloud; generated by demo/scripts/voiceover.py)

Total video length 1:24. Numbers are spoken from `demo/out/numbers.json`, so they match the screen. Rebuild the video (`make video`) and rerun the generator if the numbers change.

| Time | Shot | Fits? | Read this |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0:00 to 0:07 | Hook (7 s) | about 5 s of speech, ok | Is NEAR Intents real settlement? And does it create value for NEAR? |
| 0:07 to 0:15 | Overview (8 s) | about 7 s of speech, ok | Short answer: real infrastructure, thin value for the token. Every figure shows its date range. |
| 0:15 to 0:32 | Daily volume (17 s) | about 15 s of speech, ok | 1.3 billion dollars of net swap volume, September 29th to October 28th, read straight from the intents dot near logs. About 35 percent of reported volume isn't in public events: implied confidential, inferred, not measured. |
| 0:32 to 0:49 | Accounts (17 s) | about 13 s of speech, ok | 99.96 percent of 4.2 million implicit accounts are used on one day only. In October, just 0.22 percent were active twice or more. So account counts can't prove adoption. |
| 0:49 to 1:04 | Value capture (15 s) | about 11 s of speech, ok | Captured revenue is 26.2 million dollars a year, 0.43 percent of NEAR's market cap. Even at ten times today's volume, it would be 4.28 percent. |
| 1:04 to 1:16 | Terminal (12 s) | about 6 s of speech, ok | One command re-runs the whole thesis. No accounts, no keys. The numbers don't move. |
| 1:16 to 1:24 | Outro (8 s) | about 3 s of speech, ok | NearQuery. Ask the chain. Show the work. |

## How to record

- Start each line when its shot starts (the Time column); finish a beat before the next shot. A short pause is fine: the picture holds on the chart.
- Say the numbers slowly; they are on screen for the whole shot. Do not speed up to fit.
- Dots in "intents dot near" are spoken, not written. "NEAR" is one word.
- Record each shot as its own take, so a slip means redoing eight seconds, not the whole video.
- The terminal clip is sped up (the badge says so); talk at your normal pace over it.
- Quiet room, mic about a hand's width from your mouth, soft furnishings nearby. Do a test take and listen with headphones.

## Add it to the video

With iMovie: import the video and your takes, drop each take at its start time, export 1080p. Or with ffmpeg, from one file `voice.wav` made the length of the video:

```
ffmpeg -i demo/out/nearquery-demo-nocaptions.mp4 -i voice.wav -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 192k -shortest demo/out/nearquery-demo-voice.mp4
```
